objective: Stop ongoing, non-recoverable intraday data loss and corruption at the point of capture: unify KIS/LS vendor semantics into one canonical schema, make silent tick truncation explicit, replace destructive partition overwrite with merge, extend the archive target set to the T-1 watchlist (exit-path measurement), and persist the full 10-level orderbook ladder + closing-auction expected-fill series that the pipeline currently fetches and discards.

evidence.A_unit_collision: data/history/intraday/1m/regular/2026-09/2026-09-03.parquet (KIS) acml_tr_pbmn=738988315 is CUMULATIVE KRW; 2026-09-04.parquet (LS) acml_tr_pbmn is per-bar and in MILLIONS of KRW -- measured close*volume/value median = 1,001,385. src/api/ls/client.py::_normalize_bar line 27 maps LS 'value' onto the KIS name 'acml_tr_pbmn'. Same collision for acml_vol (LS maps per-bar jdiff_vol onto the cumulative KIS name).
evidence.B_schema_drift: 485 partition files: 484 carry 10 columns (stck_bsop_date,...), 1 carries 22 columns (date,time,open,... plus KIS aliases). read_intraday_range concatenates them into a ragged frame.
evidence.C_tick_truncation: src/api/ls/client.py::get_tick_chart max_pages=100 x qrycnt=500 = 50,000 tick hard cap, paged newest-to-oldest. On 2026-09-04, 7 of 23 symbols hit the cap and lost their morning session: 032940 starts at 13:35:44, 108490 at 10:49:52, 336260 at 10:05:06, 030530 at 11:48:40, 014950 at 12:17:25. Non-backfillable TR, so the loss is permanent and currently silent.
evidence.D_gapfill_inversion: LS t8412 emits a continuous 381-bar series, filling no-trade minutes with volume=0 and a carried price (009900 09:01-09:02 close=7770 vol=0 while the first real print is 09:03 @9100). KIS FHKST03010200 omits no-trade minutes entirely. Opposite gap-fill semantics under one column set.
evidence.E_overwrite_asymmetry: src/daily/archive_intraday.py calls write_intraday_partition (full overwrite) while src/backfill/intraday/backfill_minute_history.py::_merge_and_write_partition merges. Re-running the evening archive after a backfill silently deletes backfilled symbols.
evidence.G_ls_lock: src/api/ls/client.py::_post_tr holds self._lock across the HTTP round-trip and resp.json(), so Semaphore(10) in the collector is fully negated; effective throughput is 1/(1.05 + RTT) instead of 1/1.05.
evidence.I_orderbook_discarded: src/daily/collect.py::_parse_orderbook keeps only askp1/bidp1/total_askp_rsqn/total_bidp_rsqn from the FHKST01010200 (inquire-asking-price-exp-ccn) response that is ALREADY being fetched twice per symbol per day. The full depth ladder and the expected-fill block in the same payload are dropped at zero API cost.
evidence.I_auction_hole: Every KIS-era 1m partition is structurally missing bars 152000-152900 (no continuous trades during the closing auction). The strategy decides at ~15:18 and its fill prints in that auction, so the single most decision-relevant 10 minutes has no data at all.
evidence.J_exit_path: src/ml/exit_policy.py::attach_next_day_path consumes only daily OHLC (nd_open/nd_high/nd_low/nd_close). archive_intraday collects bars for date T scoped to T's watchlist only, so the T+1 morning path of positions actually held is never captured and take-profit fill probability cannot be measured.

assumptions_and_invariants: Raw-layer fidelity: this contract normalizes NAMES, UNITS and DTYPES only. No column is dropped because it looks derivable, and no value is rounded. Vendor-specific extra fields are carried as nullable canonical columns, never silently discarded.

The orderbook/auction store persists the vendor payload key-for-key. Field names inside the KIS FHKST01010200 output1 block are NOT enumerated in this contract because they have not been empirically probed on this account; the implementation must copy whatever keys the response carries. Do not invent field names.
value_krw is always per-bar (incremental) and always in KRW. KIS cumulative acml_tr_pbmn is converted by a per-symbol, time-ordered first difference; LS per-bar value is multiplied by 1_000_000.
has_trade = (volume > 0). It exists to make LS synthetic zero-volume bars distinguishable from KIS trade-only bars, so downstream code can choose either gap-fill convention without re-deriving it.

Tick truncation is surfaced, not fixed. Full REST tick capture is not achievable inside the batch window (727,290 ticks for 23 symbols = 1,455 pages x 1.05s pacing ~= 25 minutes). Raising the cap alone would blow the window, so the cap becomes configurable and cap-hits are recorded per symbol as truncated=True plus a warning, ending the silent loss.
Partition writes become merge-by-key everywhere (union of existing and new, keep=last). A write is never allowed to reduce a partition's symbol coverage.

The closing-auction poller is a standalone, read-only CLI. It places no orders and does not touch collect.py/predict.py control flow, so it can be started or skipped on any given day without affecting execution.
Previous trading day is resolved from data (max archive snapshot date strictly less than snapshot_date), never from a calendar offset, so market holidays cannot produce an empty T-1 set.
out_of_scope: Migration of the 485 existing partition files into the canonical schema (follow-up spec: intraday_corpus_migration).
zstd re-compression and dtype downcasting of price_history.parquet / altdata panels (follow-up spec).
Switching tick routing preference from LS back to KIS. The canonical tick schema reserves nullable trade_strength/ask1/bid1 columns so that decision can be made later without another schema change.
VI trigger log and KRX 시간외단일가 capture.

requirements.rule: normalize_bar_frame is fail-closed on vendor. vendor not in {'kis','ls'} raises ValueError. A missing required source column raises ValueError -- never partially fill and never silently return an empty frame.
requirements.detail: KIS source keys: stck_cntg_hour->ts_hms, stck_oprc->open, stck_hgpr->high, stck_lwpr->low, stck_prpr->close, cntg_vol->volume, acml_tr_pbmn->(cumulative KRW). LS source keys: time->ts_hms, open/high/low/close as-is, jdiff_vol->volume, value->(per-bar, millions KRW). An empty input frame returns an empty frame carrying exactly CANONICAL_BAR_COLUMNS with the canonical dtypes (this is a no-op, not an error).

requirements.rule: value_krw is ALWAYS per-bar and in KRW. For vendor='kis', sort the frame by ts_hms ascending and take the first difference of the cumulative acml_tr_pbmn, with the first bar keeping the raw cumulative value. For vendor='ls', value_krw = value * LS_VALUE_UNIT_KRW.
requirements.detail: A negative difference (duplicate or out-of-order source rows) is clamped to 0 and logged once per symbol via logger.warning with the [DATA] tag. This is the single defect that makes the KIS-era and LS-era corpora numerically incomparable, so it must be covered by an explicit test.

requirements.rule: has_trade = volume > 0, computed after numeric coercion. LS synthetic no-trade bars (volume==0 with a carried price) therefore land as has_trade=False while every KIS bar lands as has_trade=True.
requirements.detail: The bar row is retained either way -- do NOT drop zero-volume rows. Dropping them would destroy the LS continuous-series property, which is itself information.

requirements.rule: Canonical dtypes are exact and enforced: snapshot_date=str(YYYY-MM-DD), symbol=str zero-filled to 6, ts_hms=int32 (HHMMSS as an integer), open/high/low/close=int32 (KRW is integral), volume=int64, value_krw=int64, has_trade=bool, vendor=str. Tick: price=int32, volume=int64, trade_strength=float32 nullable, ask1/bid1=Int32 nullable, truncated=bool, vendor=str.
requirements.detail: Column ORDER must equal CANONICAL_BAR_COLUMNS / CANONICAL_TICK_COLUMNS exactly. trade_strength/ask1/bid1 come from the KIS tick TR (tday_rltv/askp/bidp) when present and are left null for LS -- they are reserved so a future routing switch needs no schema change.

requirements.rule: assert_canonical_bars / assert_canonical_ticks raise ValueError naming the offending columns when the column set or order does not match the canonical tuple. They are no-ops for an empty frame that still carries the canonical columns.
requirements.detail: These are the fail-closed gate used by intraday_store writes.

requirements.rule: Delete _normalize_bar entirely. get_minute_chart and get_tick_chart return vendor-native LS rows untouched, and the response dict gains a top-level "vendor": "ls" key. Vendor mapping happens exactly once, in the collector, via normalize_*_frame.
requirements.detail: This is what removes the acml_tr_pbmn / acml_vol name collisions at the source. No LS field may be written under a KIS field name anywhere.

requirements.rule: _post_tr must hold self._lock ONLY for the pacing computation and the _last_call_time stamp. The session.post call, the response context manager, and resp.json() must all execute outside the lock.
requirements.detail: Pacing semantics are unchanged (>= self._min_interval between request starts); only the serialization of the network round-trip is removed. The LS per-TR rate limit is ~1 req/s, so _min_interval stays 1.05 -- do not lower it.

requirements.rule: get_tick_chart takes max_pages: int | None = None, resolving to settings.LS_TICK_MAX_PAGES (new setting, default 100) when None. When the loop exits because the page budget was exhausted rather than because 09:00 was reached, the response must carry "truncated": True and log a logger.warning with the [DATA] tag naming the symbol, the page count, and the earliest time actually captured.
requirements.detail: Fail-loud, not fail-silent: an untruncated result carries "truncated": False. The cap is deliberately NOT raised by default -- 100 pages already costs ~105s/symbol at 1.05s pacing, and the operator now has both the knob and the visibility to make that trade-off. Never return a partially-captured series without the flag.

requirements.rule: Every _fetch_one path (LS bars, KIS bars, LS ticks, KIS ticks, historical backfill bars) must return an ALREADY-CANONICAL frame produced by normalize_bar_frame / normalize_tick_frame with the vendor that actually served the row. Only then may the per-symbol frames be concatenated.
requirements.detail: Because routing falls back per symbol, a mixed-vendor day is normal; normalizing before concat is what keeps the day's partition homogeneous. Drop the '종목코드'/'스냅샷_날짜' raw-tagging lines -- symbol/snapshot_date are now set by the normalizer. The truncated flag from get_tick_chart is threaded into normalize_tick_frame.

requirements.rule: write_intraday_partition and write_tick_partition must (a) call the matching assert_canonical_* gate, (b) merge with any existing partition via merge_partition_frame instead of overwriting, and (c) return the row count of the MERGED frame.
requirements.detail: merge_partition_frame concatenates existing+new, drops duplicates on key_cols keeping the last (new wins), and sorts by key_cols. Bar keys = ('symbol','ts_hms'); tick keys = ('symbol','ts_hms','volume'). It must also assert that the merged symbol set is a superset of the existing symbol set and raise ValueError otherwise -- a write may never reduce partition coverage. A missing or unreadable existing partition degrades to 'new only' with a warning, never to an exception.

requirements.rule: build_orderbook_rows copies the vendor payload key-for-key. It reads res['output1'] (dict) and emits ONE row containing capture_ts, symbol, venue, capture_reason plus every key of output1 verbatim. Values are coerced with pd.to_numeric(errors='coerce') only when the raw string is fully numeric; otherwise the original string is kept.
requirements.detail: Do NOT enumerate, rename, or whitelist KIS field names -- the whole point is capturing the full depth ladder and expected-fill block whose exact keys have not been probed on this account. res with rt_cd != '0' or a non-dict output1 yields an empty list (fail-closed, no exception). capture_reason is one of 'decision' or 'auction'.

requirements.rule: append_orderbook_snapshots writes data/history/orderbook/{YYYY-MM}/{YYYY-MM-DD}.parquet, merging with any existing partition on ('capture_ts','symbol','venue') keep=last, and returns the merged row count. An empty rows list is a 0-return no-op.
requirements.detail: Column union across appends is expected and allowed at this raw layer (a later sweep may carry keys an earlier one did not); reindex to the sorted union and leave gaps null. capture_ts is a tz-aware Asia/Seoul timestamp.

requirements.rule: fetch_single_stock returns a 3-tuple (row_dict, failed_apis, orderbook_rows). The existing four flattened columns (krx_매도호가1/krx_매수호가1/krx_매도잔량/krx_매수잔량 and the NXT pair) stay exactly as they are for archive/GSheet backward compatibility; orderbook_rows additionally carries the FULL raw output1 for both venues via build_orderbook_rows.
requirements.detail: ARCHIVE_COLUMN_ORDER and STANDARD_COLUMN_ORDER must NOT be widened -- the depth ladder goes to the orderbook partition, not into the flat archive row that syncs to GSheet. fetch_all_stock_data collects the per-symbol lists and calls append_orderbook_snapshots ONCE with capture_reason='decision'. A store write failure is logged and swallowed: orderbook capture must never break the live decision path.

requirements.rule: resolve_previous_archive_date returns the greatest archive snapshot date strictly less than snapshot_date, or None when there is none. _archive_target_codes returns the deduplicated union of the watchlists for snapshot_date and that previous date.
requirements.detail: Derive the previous session from the archive's own date index, never from a calendar offset -- holidays and weekends must not yield an empty T-1 set. Rationale: positions opened on T-1 are exited on T's morning, so T's bar partition must cover them or take-profit fill probability stays unmeasurable (exit_policy currently sees only daily OHLC). An archive read failure degrades to today-only with a warning, never to an exception.

requirements.rule: run_auction_capture polls get_orderbook_snapshot(market_div_code='J') for every watchlist symbol once per interval_seconds while start_hm <= now < end_hm, appending each sweep with capture_reason='auction'. It returns the total number of rows appended.
requirements.detail: now_fn (default datetime.now) and client are injectable so the loop is testable without wall-clock sleeps or network. An empty watchlist returns 0 without entering the loop. A failed sweep is logged and the loop continues -- partial auction coverage beats none, because this window is structurally absent from every minute-bar partition (no continuous trades during 동시호가) and is not backfillable by any TR. main() is a CLI accepting --date/--interval/--start/--end; it must not be wired into collect.py or predict.py.

requirements.rule: Add LS_TICK_MAX_PAGES: int = 100 and ORDERBOOK_DIR (computed_field returning HISTORY_DIR / 'orderbook') following the existing pydantic-settings/computed_field conventions in the file, and re-export both through src/config/__init__.py alongside HISTORY_DIR.

tests/unit/data/test_intraday_store.py currently writes non-canonical frames ({'종목코드','stck_prpr'}) and WILL fail against the R10 gate. Rewrite those three tests to build canonical frames; do not weaken or remove the gate to keep them green.
requirements.detail: Same for any collector/archive_intraday test asserting the old raw column names or the 2-tuple return of fetch_single_stock.

cli_entrypoints.self_wiring: main() parses argparse args and calls run_auction_capture(snapshot_date=args.date, interval_seconds=args.interval, start_hm=args.start, end_hm=args.end); this is the ONLY caller by design (R15) -- it must not be chained into collect.py or predict.py.

def test_normalize_bar_frame_ls_value_is_scaled_to_krw_per_bar() -> None:
    import pandas as pd

    from src.data.intraday_schema import normalize_bar_frame

    # Given: 실측 LS t8412 응답 행 (2026-09-04, 009900)
    raw = pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "time": ["090300", "090400"],
            "open": [9100, 9210],
            "high": [9100, 9210],
            "low": [9100, 9210],
            "close": [9100, 9210],
            "jdiff_vol": [55226, 108719],
            "value": [498, 998],
        }
    )

    # When
    out = normalize_bar_frame(raw, "ls", "2026-09-04", "009900")

    # Then
    assert out["value_krw"].tolist() == [498_000_000, 998_000_000]
    notional = out["close"].iloc[0] * out["volume"].iloc[0]
    assert abs(out["value_krw"].iloc[0] - notional) / notional < 0.01
    assert out["symbol"].tolist() == ["009900", "009900"]
    assert out["snapshot_date"].tolist() == ["2026-09-04", "2026-09-04"]

def test_normalize_tick_frame_carries_truncated_flag_and_optional_kis_fields() -> None:
    import pandas as pd

    from src.data.intraday_schema import CANONICAL_TICK_COLUMNS, normalize_tick_frame

    ls_raw = pd.DataFrame({"time": ["090247", "090248"], "close": [8990, 9000], "jdiff_vol": [30301, 45]})
    ls_out = normalize_tick_frame(ls_raw, "ls", "2026-09-04", "009900", truncated=True)

    assert list(ls_out.columns) == list(CANONICAL_TICK_COLUMNS)
    assert ls_out["price"].tolist() == [8990, 9000]
    assert ls_out["truncated"].all()
    assert ls_out["trade_strength"].isna().all()

    kis_raw = pd.DataFrame(
        {"stck_cntg_hour": ["090247"], "stck_prpr": ["8990"], "cnqn": ["30301"], "tday_rltv": ["120.5"], "askp": ["9000"], "bidp": ["8990"]}
    )
    kis_out = normalize_tick_frame(kis_raw, "kis", "2026-09-04", "009900")

    assert kis_out["truncated"].tolist() == [False]
    assert float(kis_out["trade_strength"].iloc[0]) == 120.5
    assert int(kis_out["ask1"].iloc[0]) == 9000
    assert int(kis_out["bid1"].iloc[0]) == 8990

def test_ls_get_tick_chart_marks_truncated_when_page_budget_exhausted() -> None:
    import asyncio

    from src.api.ls.client import LsApiClient

    client = LsApiClient(app_key="k", app_secret="s")
    client.token = "t"
    client._min_interval = 0.0

    calls = {"n": 0}

    async def fake_post_tr(session, tr_cd, tr_key, body, tr_cont="N", tr_cont_key="", max_retries=3):
        calls["n"] += 1
        # 항상 09:00 이전에 도달하지 못하는 응답 -- 페이지 예산 소진을 강제한다
        rows = [{"date": "20260904", "time": "143000", "close": 100, "jdiff_vol": 1}]
        return ({"rsp_cd": "00000", "t8411OutBlock1": rows, "t8411OutBlock": {"cts_date": "20260904", "cts_time": "142959"}}, {"tr_cont": "Y", "tr_cont_key": "x"})

    client._post_tr = fake_post_tr

    res = asyncio.run(client.get_tick_chart(object(), "005930", "2026-09-04", max_pages=3))

    assert res["rt_cd"] == "0"
    assert res["truncated"] is True
    assert calls["n"] == 3
    assert res["vendor"] == "ls"

    from datetime import datetime

    import pandas as pd

    monkeypatch.setattr(
        collect_auction.archive,

    clock = iter(
        [
